tldr: No direct Canadian competitor moved on product today; RBC Insurance's Men's Health Program was the only item from the named peer set, and it is a benefits play. The news that matters comes from the edges: tokenized stocks, AI-agent checkout, extended-hours trading and US charters for digital lenders, plus Latin American card-rewards and fee changes.
themes: AI agents in payments and analytics
Card rewards and Black Friday promos
Fees and friction on funding and accounts

highlights.headline: OKX and NYSE parent ICE launch a tokenized stock venue with 113 assets lined up, while Nasdaq publishes a 23/5 trading information hub.
highlights.why: Tokenized equities and near-round-the-clock trading are becoming mainstream exchange offerings, which will raise customer expectations for Simplii's self-directed trading hours and asset access.

highlights.headline: Klarna is now available inside Adyen's AI agent checkout (Adyen Agentic), and Expensify launched AI-powered Insights analytics.
highlights.why: Payments and spend tools are starting to build in agent-led purchasing and AI analysis of spending, which gives Simplii a reference point for how AI could show up in its payments and money-management features.

highlights.headline: Payoneer received preliminary OCC approval for a stablecoin national trust bank, and OakNorth secured a US national banking charter.
highlights.why: Fintechs are gaining regulated status and stablecoin infrastructure. This is a category shift that points to more regulated, low-cost cross-border and digital-bank rivals.

highlights.headline: RBC Insurance launched a Men's Health Program, extending its personalized Group Benefit Solutions.
highlights.why: It's the only item from a named Canadian peer, and it shows RBC deepening its employer-benefits and wellness offering beyond core banking. It's worth a quick look, though it has little direct bearing on Simplii's retail products.
